findings.summary: `api.undo()` / `api.redo()` bypass the new read-only guard applied to both key paths
findings.evidence: The diff deliberately withholds history from read-only mounts in two places: `historyKeymap` is `[]` when `readOnly` (editor.ts:213-214, "Read-only mounts get no binding at all — the document is not writable") and the vim route falls through unless `cm.cm6.state.facet(EditorView.editable)` (editor.ts:52). But the third entry point, `NoteEditorAPI.undo/redo` (editor.ts:431-438), calls `runHistory(...)` -> `store[kind]()` with no `readOnly` check at all, so a host that surfaces an undo affordance on a read-only mount writes reverse ops into the CRDT (which the auth webhook then rejects, or worse, applies for a viewer that does hold write scope on the doc). The in-repo caller happens to hide the buttons (`notes-toolbar.tsx:200` `canFormat = !readOnly && ...`), so this is currently latent, but `NoteEditorAPI` is exported from the package and the guard belongs with the other two.

findings.summary: Undo no longer restores the caret to the edit site; the reverted text arrives as a remote transaction with only mapped selection
findings.evidence: The old path used @codemirror/commands' `undo`, which restores the selection recorded with the history event. The replacement (`historyKeymap`, editor.ts:209-238, "minus the selection-undo entries (Yorkie has no selection history)") routes to `store.undo()`, whose result comes back through `subscribeRemote` and is applied by `note-sync.applyRemote` as a plain `remote`-annotated transaction — CodeMirror only *maps* the existing selection through it. So undoing an edit made off-screen leaves the caret and viewport where they are, with no visible indication of what was reverted. `YorkieDocStore` solves exactly this by writing the pre-edit caret into Yorkie history via `recordHistoryPresence` with `{ addToHistory: true }` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2683-2695); `YorkieNoteStore` has no equivalent. Searched: yorkie-note-store.ts (whole file), note-sync.ts applyRemote, editor.ts runHistory/historyKeymap, grep for addToHistory/recordHistoryPresence across packages/frontend/src.

findings.summary: `undoFloor` is an absolute stack depth compared against a Yorkie stack that can shrink independently (cap eviction / snapshot reset), so undo can silently stop early
findings.evidence: `canUndo()` requires `doc.getUndoStackForTest().length > this.undoFloor` with `undoFloor` frozen at construction (line 49). That is only sound if the stack never loses entries below the floor. In a text editor one CodeMirror transaction = one Yorkie change (per this PR's own design), so the stack grows one entry per keystroke and will hit Yorkie's stack bound; likewise a snapshot applied mid-session can reset it. Once the entries the floor was counting are gone, the comparison no longer means "above the seed" — it just refuses the user's oldest `undoFloor` genuine edits (or, after a reset, blocks undo entirely until the depth climbs back past the floor). A floor recorded as an identity/marker of the seed change rather than a raw depth would not have this failure mode. Same shape exists in the slides/docs/board stores, so this is a pattern-level risk, not one this PR invented — but it is newly load-bearing here because notes push far more undo units than those stores.

findings.summary: MemNoteStore keeps an unbounded stack of full-text snapshots and replaces the whole document on undo
findings.evidence: `pushUndo` (memory.ts, `private pushUndo`) appends a full copy of the note text on every un-batched `editText` and every mutating `batch`, with no cap and no eviction — one whole-document string per keystroke, retained for the life of the store. The class comment justifies it as "cheap enough for a note", which is only true for short sessions. Separately, `undo()`/`redo()` emit `{ type: 'replace', content }`, which `note-sync.applyRemote` turns into a `from: 0, to: doc.length` replacement of the entire document — that discards CodeMirror's per-change mapping (selection/scroll land wherever a whole-doc replace maps them) where the Yorkie store emits precise `edits`. Impact is bounded today because MemNoteStore is only referenced from tests and the package export surface (grep: only editor.test.ts, note-sync.test.ts, memory.test.ts, index.ts, node.ts).

findings.summary: History keybindings swallow Mod-z / Mod-Shift-z even when there is nothing to undo or redo
findings.evidence: Each `run` in the new `historyKeymap` (editor.ts:216-237) unconditionally `return true` after calling `runHistory(...)`, and `store.undo()`/`redo()` no-op when `canUndo()`/`canRedo()` is false. @codemirror/commands' `undo` returns false in that case, letting the key fall through. Consequence is small (the key is consumed and preventDefault'd with no effect) but it is a behavior change from the command this replaced.

findings.summary: Design doc (and matching code/test comments) justify the batching design with an inaccurate example: `insertTable` is not a multi-change command
findings.evidence: notes.md:278 — "a command that dispatches several changes (e.g. `insertTable`) undoes in a single step"; note-sync.ts:58 repeats it ("a command that dispatches several, e.g. insertTable"), and notes-undo-integration.test.ts's header calls insertTable "one CodeMirror transaction carrying several changes". In packages/notes/src/view/commands.ts:176 `insertTable` issues a single `view.dispatch` with a single `changes: { from: pos, insert: table }`. Every note command (toggleWrap, toggleLink, insertTable) dispatches exactly one transaction, and the only multi-change one is the unwrap branch of toggleWrap (commands.ts:75). The canonical design record therefore documents a motivation the code does not exhibit; a reader can't tell whether ViewUpdate-level batching is actually needed or what it is protecting.

findings.summary: Vim history routing is done by permanently overwriting a third-party module global (`CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo`) from `initialize()`, rather than through the vim adapter's own extension points
findings.evidence: `routeVimHistoryToStore()` mutates `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo` process-wide on first `initialize()` and never restores them on `dispose()`. The engine package is a library; a module-global patch of a dependency's command table is a wrong-layer abstraction — @replit/codemirror-vim exposes `Vim.defineAction` / `mapCommand`, and the keymap compartment already exists for per-view bindings. It happens to be safe today only because notes is the sole consumer of codemirror-vim (grep: only packages/notes references it), and the design doc itself records that the sibling `:undo`/`:redo` ex-commands are left permanently inert as a consequence.

findings.summary: Undo granularity regresses to one unit per CodeMirror transaction (per keystroke) for a plain-text editor; the issue did not ask for dropping keystroke coalescing
findings.evidence: notes.md:303-306 records the behavior change: "CodeMirror grouped keystrokes into a time window (`newGroupDelay`), while Yorkie's unit is the change — so undo now steps per CodeMirror transaction." For a markdown text editor this is a materially worse undo UX than for Slides/Docs object edits, and the originating issue's outcome is only "multi-user undo"; nothing required abandoning coalescing. The task doc lists coalescing as out of scope, so this is a scope/UX trade-off call worth confirming rather than a criterion failure.

findings.summary: The two NoteStore implementations now diverge observably on undo: MemNoteStore emits a whole-document `replace`, YorkieNoteStore emits incremental `edits`
findings.evidence: MemNoteStore.undo/redo emit `{ type: 'replace', content }` (memory.ts:56, 64), which noteSync applies as a full 0..doc.length replacement (note-sync.ts:32-38), resetting selection/decorations; YorkieNoteStore's undo arrives as incremental `edits`. The interface doc in store.ts:54-58 describes one contract for both. Slides deliberately kept MemSlidesStore on snapshot undo (slides-native-undo.md:44-47), so precedent exists, but the notes engine's non-collaborative path (`src/node.ts` exports MemNoteStore as the public store) now behaves differently from production under the same API.

findings.summary: Undo floor is capture-at-construction only; unlike Slides/Docs there is no `markUndoBaseline()` re-base hook, so a store rebuilt over an already-edited doc silently discards the user's undo history
findings.evidence: `this.undoFloor = doc.getUndoStackForTest().length` in the constructor is the only capture. YorkieSlidesStore exposes `markUndoBaseline()` (yorkie-slides-store.ts:669) called from slides-view.tsx:648 after a post-construction seed, and YorkieDocStore re-bases in `setDocument` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:732). notes-view.tsx:93 constructs the store in an effect keyed on `[didMount, doc]`; if that effect ever re-runs against the same live doc after local edits, the new floor sits above the user's own units and `canUndo()` returns false for work they can still see. Whether that re-mount can happen today is unclear, hence low confidence — but the missing re-base hook is the divergence from the pattern the issue said to reuse.

findings.summary: Fourth copy of the ambient-root / batchDepth / undoFloor Yorkie-undo pattern with no shared helper extracted
findings.evidence: Identical structure now exists in yorkie-slides-store.ts (347-358, 654), yorkie-doc-store.ts (514-529, 2557), yorkie-board-store.ts (221-230, 438-442) and this file. The repo expects reuse via @wafflebase/core, but core contains none of this today (grep for undoFloor/activeRoot/history.undo under packages/core/src returned nothing), so following the copy convention is defensible — flagging only that the duplication has now crossed four stores and is a candidate for extraction.
searchedFor: glob docs/design/**/*.md for a shared-undo doc

findings.summary: New vim history routing (`routeVimHistoryToStore`) has no test at all
findings.evidence: editor.ts:28-60 adds a global monkey-patch of `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo` so vim's `u` / `<C-r>` reach `store.undo()/redo()`, including a read-only fall-through branch (`cm.cm6.state.facet(EditorView.editable)`). Grepping the whole notes package for `vim`/`CodeMirror.commands` shows the only vim test is `editor.test.ts:156 'switches the keybinding mode (default <-> vim)'`, which only asserts `api.getKeymap()` and text preservation — it never presses `u`, never invokes `CodeMirror.commands.undo`, and never checks the store's history moved. So the whole routing function, its facet lookup, its editable guard and its `defaultVimHistory` fall-through can break silently. Since CodeMirror's own history is now disabled, a regression here means vim users lose undo entirely with a green suite.

findings.summary: setLocalSelection folding into an open batch (activeRoot/activePresence path) is untested
findings.evidence: The diff adds a new branch in `setLocalSelection` (yorkie-note-store.ts:187-193) that publishes presence against the batch's ambient root/presence instead of opening a nested `doc.update`, plus the `activePresence` field whose doc claims 'Presence is not added to history, so it never pollutes the batch's undo unit'. Neither claim is exercised: `yorkie-note-store.test.ts` (read in full) has no test calling `setLocalSelection` inside `store.batch(...)`, and the only existing selection assertion is `getPeerSelections()` for a single client. The new integration test mounts the editor but never asserts anything about presence, and the remote-selection plugin publishes from its own ViewUpdate outside noteSync's batch, so the folding path is likely never hit there either. If the branch were wrong (e.g. nested-update throw, or presence landing in the undo unit) nothing would fail.
searchedFor: read notes-undo-integration.test.ts in diff for presence assertions

findings.summary: `runHistory`'s toolbar refresh (selectionCb after undo/redo) is not asserted anywhere
findings.evidence: `runHistory` (editor.ts ~200-206) deliberately calls `selectionCb?.(computeActiveFormats(view.state))` after `store[kind]()`, with a comment explaining the docChanged listener alone is not enough. No test in editor.test.ts registers `onSelectionChange` and then calls `api.undo()`/`api.redo()` to assert the callback fires, so this deliberate extra notification could be deleted without any test failing.

findings.summary: 'leaves history unbound on a read-only mount' is a negative test with no positive control
findings.evidence: The test dispatches a Ctrl-z keydown on `.cm-content` of a read-only mount and asserts `store.getText()` is unchanged. Nothing in the test proves the synthetic keydown would ever have reached CodeMirror's keymap on this mount (no focus, editable=false, jsdom); the assertion also holds if the event is simply ignored for unrelated reasons, so it does not specifically demonstrate that `historyKeymap: readOnly ? [] : ...` is what suppressed the undo. It also never covers the vim read-only fall-through added in editor.ts:52-56.

findings.summary: The `Mod-y` redo binding is never exercised
findings.evidence: The new historyKeymap adds three entries: `Mod-z`, `{key:'Mod-y', mac:'Mod-Shift-z'}` and `Mod-Shift-z`. The test 'binds Mod-z / Mod-Shift-z to the store history' (editor.test.ts:107) only presses Ctrl-z and Ctrl-Shift-z; no test presses Ctrl-y, so the Mod-y entry has zero coverage.

findings.summary: MemNoteStore's new unsubscribe (listener removal) is untested
findings.evidence: `subscribeRemote` changed from a no-op returning `() => {}` to a real listener registry with a removing unsubscribe (memory.ts:78-83). memory.test.ts's new 'emits the reverted text to remote subscribers' test never calls the returned unsubscribe and then asserts no further events, so a broken unsubscribe (leaked listener) would pass.

findings.summary: Write-capable undo()/redo() have no read-only/permission gate; the read-only check lives only in the two view-level callers
findings.evidence: `YorkieNoteStore.undo()` (yorkie-note-store.ts:93) calls `doc.history.undo()`, which mutates the shared CRDT, and neither the store nor `NoteEditorAPI.undo()` (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:431) consults `readOnly`. The only things stopping a viewer-role share session from writing are two view-level gates: the history keymap is replaced by `[]` when `readOnly` (editor.ts:213) and the vim route checks `EditorView.editable` (editor.ts:52), plus the toolbar hiding the buttons behind `canFormat = !readOnly && mode !== 'view'` (notes-toolbar.tsx:200). Attack chain: a viewer opens a shared note (shared-document.tsx:288 sets `readOnly = resolved.role === 'viewer'`, line 310 mounts NotesView with it) and any caller reaching `api.undo()` — a future toolbar/menu/shortcut wired without re-checking readOnly, or a keymap switch to vim on a mount whose editable facet changes — writes reverse ops into the document. Server-side the Yorkie auth webhook would reject an `rw` PushPull, but only once `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true'`; the default is shadow mode, which logs and allows (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:97-105), so such a write persists. I found no currently reachable caller, hence low confidence; the gap is that the enforcement point is not on the operation that writes. Existing stores (yorkie-slides-store.ts:632, yorkie-doc-store.ts) share this shape, so it is a pattern-level gap rather than a new one.
searchedFor: grep NotesView|NotesToolbar across packages/frontend/src (shared-document.tsx:310 is the only readOnly mount)
read packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts (historyKeymap readOnly branch, vim route editable check)
grep readOnly|canEdit in packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts (no store-level gate there either)
read packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts (server-side rw enforcement + shadow mode default)

findings.summary: Remote edit ops are matched by path prefix (startsWith('$.content')), so a peer's ops on a sibling root key are applied to the local editor
findings.evidence: `subscribeRemote` applies any op whose `path` merely starts with `$.content` (yorkie-note-store.ts:153). Yorkie roots are schemaless, so a collaborator with write access (workspace member, or an `editor`-role share visitor — yorkie-auth.controller.ts:200) can do `root.contentX = new Text(); root.contentX.edit(...)`; the resulting `edit` op has path `$.contentX`, passes the prefix test, and is dispatched into this client's CodeMirror doc (note-sync.ts:43). The victim's view then diverges from `root.content`, and their next keystroke is translated with corrupted coordinates and written back to the real content, corrupting the note for every peer. Requires an already-authorized writer, so impact is integrity-only. The line predates this diff (only the comment above it changed), but the new undo path now flows through the same handler. Fix: compare `=== '$.content'` or anchor on `$.content.`.

findings.summary: MemNoteStore's undo/redo stacks grow without bound, one full text snapshot per edit
findings.evidence: `pushUndo` (memory.ts:97) appends a complete copy of the document text on every edit and the stacks are never trimmed, so N edits on an M-byte note retain O(N*M) bytes for the process lifetime — a client-side memory-exhaustion vector if MemNoteStore is ever mounted on user-supplied content. Today `grep MemNoteStore` finds only test files plus the `packages/notes/src/node.ts` export, so there is no production consumer; capping the stack (as CodeMirror's history does with minDepth) would remove the hazard before one appears.
searchedFor: grep MemNoteStore across the repo (only packages/notes tests, store/memory.ts, index.ts, node.ts, docs)

findings.summary: note-sync now opens a Yorkie `doc.update` on EVERY docChanged ViewUpdate, including read-only mounts reacting to remote changes
findings.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/note-sync.ts:61 wraps the whole loop in `this.store.batch(() => {...})`, and `YorkieNoteStore.batch()` (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:76) unconditionally calls `this.doc.update(...)` before any transaction filtering. Previously, a read-only mount could never reach `doc.update` from this plugin: `editText` was only called for non-remote user-event transactions, which a non-editable view cannot produce. The out-of-diff consumer is packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:91, whose comment records the invariant that read-only share viewers must not issue writes ('a read-only share viewer has no write permission — the auth webhook would reject the update'). Now every peer edit or snapshot arriving at a read-only viewer opens a local (empty) update. Mitigating: `setLocalSelection` (remote-selection.ts:115) already calls doc.update on read-only mounts for presence, and the task note claims an empty update pushes nothing — hence low confidence. Fix belongs in YorkieNoteStore.batch (skip doc.update when nothing will be written) or in note-sync (only open a batch when at least one local transaction survives the filter).

findings.summary: Vim `u` / `<C-r>` bypass `runHistory`, so the toolbar's undo/redo enabled state is not explicitly refreshed
findings.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:52 calls `store[kind]()` directly, skipping the `runHistory` wrapper (editor.ts:205) that exists precisely because 'the resulting transaction may land before the pop is visible, so we don't rely on the docChanged listener alone'. The consumer that depends on that refresh is packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-toolbar.tsx:193, which recomputes `canUndo/canRedo` only from the selection-change callback. In vim mode the Undo/Redo buttons can therefore show stale enabled state until the next selection or doc change.

findings.summary: `canRedo()` has no floor and the Yorkie redo stack survives store reconstruction, so a remount can offer a redo belonging to a previous store instance
findings.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:113 returns raw `doc.history.canRedo()`, while `undoFloor` is re-captured per instance at yorkie-note-store.ts:49. packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:93 constructs a NEW YorkieNoteStore whenever the effect re-runs (didMount/doc), reusing the same Yorkie Document — the redo stack from the prior instance is still there, so the toolbar (notes-toolbar.tsx:193 -> editor.canRedo()) can enable Redo and re-apply an edit the current session never undid.

findings.summary: `routeVimHistoryToStore()` permanently monkey-patches the shared `@replit/codemirror-vim` module singleton for the whole process
findings.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:41-58 overwrites `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo` on the module-level singleton the first time any note editor mounts, and never restores it on `dispose()`. I grepped the repo for other `@replit/codemirror-vim` importers and found only packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:5 (plus package.json/lockfile), so nothing is broken today — but any future vim-enabled CodeMirror surface in the frontend inherits notes' routing (falling back only when `noteStoreFacet` is absent). Worth a comment/ownership note or a facet-scoped extension instead of a global patch.

findings.summary: `NoteEditorAPI.undo()/redo()` still mutate the store on a read-only mount; only the keymap path is guarded
findings.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:213 skips the history keymap when `readOnly`, and editor.ts:49-52 checks `EditorView.editable` before routing vim keys, but the public API entry points (editor.ts:431 `undo: () => runHistory('undo')`) apply no such check and reach `store.undo()` directly. The current caller, packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-toolbar.tsx:200 (`canFormat = !readOnly && mode !== 'view'`), hides the buttons, so the bypass is not reachable today — but the guard added in this change is inconsistent across entry points and a future host calling `editor.undo()` would write on a read-only share.

+# Notes native undo — lessons (issue #604)
+
+## Context
+
+Migrate WaffleNotes undo/redo from CodeMirror local history to Yorkie
+`doc.history`, so undo preserves peers' concurrent edits.
+
+## Lessons
+
+- The issue's prerequisite spike resolved cleanly: `Text.edit()` reverse
+  ops are supported on `@yorkie-js/sdk` 0.7.13. The `Tree.editByPath`
+  merge caveat that motivated the spike is a Tree-only limitation and
+  never applied to notes, whose whole content is one `Text`.
+- An empty `doc.update()` pushes nothing onto the undo stack, so
+  `batch()` does not need to pre-check whether the body will mutate.
+- Disabling `basicSetup`'s `history()` silently breaks vim's `u` /
+  `<C-r>` too: `@replit/codemirror-vim` routes them through
+  `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo`, which call `@codemirror/commands`'
+  `undo(view)` and no-op without the history extension. The static
+  `CodeMirror.commands` map is read at call time, so overriding it is
+  the supported-shaped hook; its `:undo` ex-command copy is snapshotted
+  at module load and cannot be re-routed.
+- Undo granularity changes: CM history groups keystrokes by time
+  (`newGroupDelay`), Yorkie's unit is one change. One CM transaction =
+  one undo unit, so undo now steps per keystroke — the same behavior
+  Docs and Slides already have after their migrations.

@@ -0,0 +1,81 @@
+# Notes native undo — migrate to Yorkie `doc.history` (issue #604)
+
+PR: (to be filled after opening)
+
+## Goal
+
+Move WaffleNotes undo/redo off CodeMirror's local history onto
+Yorkie-native undo (`doc.history`), so undo carries CRDT semantics and
+preserves a peer's concurrent edits instead of last-write-wins-ing over
+them. Reuses the pattern already shipped in Slides
+(`docs/design/slides/slides-native-undo.md`) and Docs
+(`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts`).
+
+## Prerequisite spike (done — result recorded here)
+
+Verified against the pinned `@yorkie-js/sdk` 0.7.13 that character-level
+`Text.edit()` **is** reversible through `doc.history`:
+
+- Two `content.edit()` calls inside ONE `doc.update()` push exactly one
+  undo-stack entry; `history.undo()` reverts both, `redo()` re-applies.
+- The undo emits a `local-change` event with `source === 'undoredo'`
+  carrying `edit` ops on `$.content` with correct `from`/`to`/`content`
+  (already reversed in apply order), i.e. the dormant `isUndoRedo` path
+  in `yorkie-note-store.ts` receives exactly what it needs.
+- A `doc.update()` whose body mutates nothing pushes **no** undo entry,
+  so an empty batch is free.
+
+(`Tree.editByPath` merge non-reversibility, called out in the issue,
+does not apply — notes store markdown in a single `Text`.)
+
+## Approach
+
+**Store layer (`packages/notes/src/store/store.ts`)** — extend
+`NoteStore` with `batch(fn)`, `undo()`, `redo()`, `canUndo()`,
+`canRedo()`. Undo becomes store-owned (like `DocStore`/`SlidesStore`)
+rather than view-owned.
+
+**`YorkieNoteStore`** — ambient-root + `withUpdate()`: a top-level
+`batch()` opens ONE `doc.update()` and every `editText()` runs against
+that ambient root, so one CodeMirror transaction group = one Yorkie
+change = one undo unit. `setLocalSelection` folds into the batch's
+ambient presence proxy when a batch is open. `undo()/redo()` delegate to
+`doc.history`, gated by an undo floor captured at construction (after
+`ensureText()` seeding) so a user cannot undo the seed away.
+
+**`MemNoteStore`** — snapshot-based local history so the engine still
+has working undo without a CRDT (tests / non-collaborative use). Undo
+emits a `replace` remote change so the view reflects it, mirroring how
+the Yorkie store's undo comes back through `subscribeRemote`.
+
+**`note-sync.ts`** — wrap the per-`ViewUpdate` `editText` loop in
+`store.batch()`.
+
+**`editor.ts`** — `basicSetup({ history: false, historyKeymap: false })`;
+bind `Mod-z` / `Mod-Shift-z` / `Mod-y` to the store (skipped in
+read-only); `NoteEditorAPI.undo/redo/canUndo/canRedo` delegate to the
+store. Vim's `u` / `<C-r>` go through `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo`,
+which the vim adapter looks up at call time — override them once to
+route to the note store resolved from the view's `noteStoreFacet`, else
+vim undo would silently no-op with CM history disabled.
+
+## Tasks
+
+- [ ] `NoteStore`: `batch` / `undo` / `redo` / `canUndo` / `canRedo`
+- [ ] `MemNoteStore`: snapshot history + `replace` emission on undo/redo
+- [ ] `YorkieNoteStore`: ambient root, `withUpdate`, batch, undo floor,
+      `doc.history` delegation
+- [ ] `note-sync.ts`: wrap local edits in `store.batch()`
+- [ ] `editor.ts`: disable CM history, history keymap → store, API
+      delegation, vim command routing
+- [ ] Tests: batch grouping = 1 undo unit, undo floor, peer-edit
+      preservation (churn regression), no-echo on undo, MemNoteStore
+      history, engine-level keybinding
+- [ ] `docs/design/notes/notes.md`: Yorkie-native undo section
+
+## Out of scope
+
+- Time-based keystroke coalescing (Yorkie's undo unit is the change;
+  Docs and Slides behave the same way).
+- `:undo` / `:redo` ex-commands in vim (the vim package snapshots those
+  handlers at module load, so they cannot be re-routed).

But the third entry point, `NoteEditorAPI.undo/redo` (editor.ts:431-438), calls `runHistory(...)` -> `store[kind]()` with no `readOnly` check at all, so a host that surfaces an undo affordance on a read-only mount writes reverse ops into the CRDT (which the auth webhook then rejects, or worse, applies for a viewer that does hold write scope on the doc). The in-repo caller happens to hide the buttons (`notes-toolbar.tsx:200` `canFormat = !readOnly && ...`), so this is currently latent, but `NoteEditorAPI` is exported from the package and the guard belongs with the other two.

samples.summary: Undo no longer restores the caret to the edit site; the reverted text arrives as a remote transaction with only mapped selection
samples.evidence: The old path used @codemirror/commands' `undo`, which restores the selection recorded with the history event. The replacement (`historyKeymap`, editor.ts:209-238, "minus the selection-undo entries (Yorkie has no selection history)") routes to `store.undo()`, whose result comes back through `subscribeRemote` and is applied by `note-sync.applyRemote` as a plain `remote`-annotated transaction — CodeMirror only *maps* the existing selection through it. So undoing an edit made off-screen leaves the caret and viewport where they are, with no visible indication of what was reverted. `YorkieDocStore` solves exactly this by writing the pre-edit caret into Yorkie history via `recordHistoryPresence` with `{ addToHistory: true }` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2683-2695); `YorkieNoteStore` has no equivalent. Searched: yorkie-note-store.ts (whole file), note-sync.ts applyRemote, editor.ts runHistory/historyKeymap, grep for addToHistory/recordHistoryPresence across packages/frontend/src.

samples.summary: `undoFloor` is an absolute stack depth compared against a Yorkie stack that can shrink independently (cap eviction / snapshot reset), so undo can silently stop early
samples.evidence: `canUndo()` requires `doc.getUndoStackForTest().length > this.undoFloor` with `undoFloor` frozen at construction (line 49). That is only sound if the stack never loses entries below the floor. In a text editor one CodeMirror transaction = one Yorkie change (per this PR's own design), so the stack grows one entry per keystroke and will hit Yorkie's stack bound; likewise a snapshot applied mid-session can reset it. Once the entries the floor was counting are gone, the comparison no longer means "above the seed" — it just refuses the user's oldest `undoFloor` genuine edits (or, after a reset, blocks undo entirely until the depth climbs back past the floor). A floor recorded as an identity/marker of the seed change rather than a raw depth would not have this failure mode. Same shape exists in the slides/docs/board stores, so this is a pattern-level risk, not one this PR invented — but it is newly load-bearing here because notes push far more undo units than those stores.

samples.summary: MemNoteStore keeps an unbounded stack of full-text snapshots and replaces the whole document on undo
samples.evidence: `pushUndo` (memory.ts, `private pushUndo`) appends a full copy of the note text on every un-batched `editText` and every mutating `batch`, with no cap and no eviction — one whole-document string per keystroke, retained for the life of the store. The class comment justifies it as "cheap enough for a note", which is only true for short sessions. Separately, `undo()`/`redo()` emit `{ type: 'replace', content }`, which `note-sync.applyRemote` turns into a `from: 0, to: doc.length` replacement of the entire document — that discards CodeMirror's per-change mapping (selection/scroll land wherever a whole-doc replace maps them) where the Yorkie store emits precise `edits`. Impact is bounded today because MemNoteStore is only referenced from tests and the package export surface (grep: only editor.test.ts, note-sync.test.ts, memory.test.ts, index.ts, node.ts).

samples.summary: History keybindings swallow Mod-z / Mod-Shift-z even when there is nothing to undo or redo
samples.evidence: Each `run` in the new `historyKeymap` (editor.ts:216-237) unconditionally `return true` after calling `runHistory(...)`, and `store.undo()`/`redo()` no-op when `canUndo()`/`canRedo()` is false. @codemirror/commands' `undo` returns false in that case, letting the key fall through. Consequence is small (the key is consumed and preventDefault'd with no effect) but it is a behavior change from the command this replaced.

samples.summary: Design doc (and matching code/test comments) justify the batching design with an inaccurate example: `insertTable` is not a multi-change command
samples.evidence: notes.md:278 — "a command that dispatches several changes (e.g. `insertTable`) undoes in a single step"; note-sync.ts:58 repeats it ("a command that dispatches several, e.g. insertTable"), and notes-undo-integration.test.ts's header calls insertTable "one CodeMirror transaction carrying several changes". In packages/notes/src/view/commands.ts:176 `insertTable` issues a single `view.dispatch` with a single `changes: { from: pos, insert: table }`. Every note command (toggleWrap, toggleLink, insertTable) dispatches exactly one transaction, and the only multi-change one is the unwrap branch of toggleWrap (commands.ts:75). The canonical design record therefore documents a motivation the code does not exhibit; a reader can't tell whether ViewUpdate-level batching is actually needed or what it is protecting.

samples.summary: Vim history routing is done by permanently overwriting a third-party module global (`CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo`) from `initialize()`, rather than through the vim adapter's own extension points
samples.evidence: `routeVimHistoryToStore()` mutates `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo` process-wide on first `initialize()` and never restores them on `dispose()`. The engine package is a library; a module-global patch of a dependency's command table is a wrong-layer abstraction — @replit/codemirror-vim exposes `Vim.defineAction` / `mapCommand`, and the keymap compartment already exists for per-view bindings. It happens to be safe today only because notes is the sole consumer of codemirror-vim (grep: only packages/notes references it), and the design doc itself records that the sibling `:undo`/`:redo` ex-commands are left permanently inert as a consequence.

samples.summary: Undo granularity regresses to one unit per CodeMirror transaction (per keystroke) for a plain-text editor; the issue did not ask for dropping keystroke coalescing
samples.evidence: notes.md:303-306 records the behavior change: "CodeMirror grouped keystrokes into a time window (`newGroupDelay`), while Yorkie's unit is the change — so undo now steps per CodeMirror transaction." For a markdown text editor this is a materially worse undo UX than for Slides/Docs object edits, and the originating issue's outcome is only "multi-user undo"; nothing required abandoning coalescing. The task doc lists coalescing as out of scope, so this is a scope/UX trade-off call worth confirming rather than a criterion failure.

samples.summary: The two NoteStore implementations now diverge observably on undo: MemNoteStore emits a whole-document `replace`, YorkieNoteStore emits incremental `edits`

The interface doc in store.ts:54-58 describes one contract for both. samples.summary: Undo floor is capture-at-construction only; unlike Slides/Docs there is no `markUndoBaseline()` re-base hook, so a store rebuilt over an already-edited doc silently discards the user's undo history
samples.evidence: `this.undoFloor = doc.getUndoStackForTest().length` in the constructor is the only capture. YorkieSlidesStore exposes `markUndoBaseline()` (yorkie-slides-store.ts:669) called from slides-view.tsx:648 after a post-construction seed, and YorkieDocStore re-bases in `setDocument` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:732). notes-view.tsx:93 constructs the store in an effect keyed on `[didMount, doc]`; if that effect ever re-runs against the same live doc after local edits, the new floor sits above the user's own units and `canUndo()` returns false for work they can still see. samples.summary: Write-capable undo()/redo() have no read-only/permission gate; the read-only check lives only in the two view-level callers
samples.evidence: `YorkieNoteStore.undo()` (yorkie-note-store.ts:93) calls `doc.history.undo()`, which mutates the shared CRDT, and neither the store nor `NoteEditorAPI.undo()` (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:431) consults `readOnly`. The only things stopping a viewer-role share session from writing are two view-level gates: the history keymap is replaced by `[]` when `readOnly` (editor.ts:213) and the vim route checks `EditorView.editable` (editor.ts:52), plus the toolbar hiding the buttons behind `canFormat = !readOnly && mode !== 'view'` (notes-toolbar.tsx:200). Attack chain: a viewer opens a shared note (shared-document.tsx:288 sets `readOnly = resolved.role === 'viewer'`, line 310 mounts NotesView with it) and any caller reaching `api.undo()` — a future toolbar/menu/shortcut wired without re-checking readOnly, or a keymap switch to vim on a mount whose editable facet changes — writes reverse ops into the document. Server-side the Yorkie auth webhook would reject an `rw` PushPull, but only once `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true'`; the default is shadow mode, which logs and allows (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:97-105), so such a write persists. I found no currently reachable caller, hence low confidence; the gap is that the enforcement point is not on the operation that writes. Existing stores (yorkie-slides-store.ts:632, yorkie-doc-store.ts) share this shape, so it is a pattern-level gap rather than a new one.

samples.summary: Remote edit ops are matched by path prefix (startsWith('$.content')), so a peer's ops on a sibling root key are applied to the local editor
samples.evidence: `subscribeRemote` applies any op whose `path` merely starts with `$.content` (yorkie-note-store.ts:153). Yorkie roots are schemaless, so a collaborator with write access (workspace member, or an `editor`-role share visitor — yorkie-auth.controller.ts:200) can do `root.contentX = new Text(); root.contentX.edit(...)`; the resulting `edit` op has path `$.contentX`, passes the prefix test, and is dispatched into this client's CodeMirror doc (note-sync.ts:43). The victim's view then diverges from `root.content`, and their next keystroke is translated with corrupted coordinates and written back to the real content, corrupting the note for every peer. Requires an already-authorized writer, so impact is integrity-only. The line predates this diff (only the comment above it changed), but the new undo path now flows through the same handler. Fix: compare `=== '$.content'` or anchor on `$.content.`.

A repo-wide grep for `.undo()`/`.redo()` yields exactly three notes entry points, all guarded: notes-toolbar.tsx:210/217 render only under `canFormat = !readOnly && mode !== "view"` (notes-toolbar.tsx:200,205) and the shared viewer layout renders no toolbar at all (shared-document.tsx:296-313); editor.ts:213 replaces the Mod-z/Mod-y keymap with `[]` when readOnly; editor.ts:52 requires the `EditorView.editable` facet, which is set once at editor.ts:287 as `!readOnly` and is never reconfigured (setKeymap touches only keymapCompartment, editor.ts:415-424; grep for `editable` in packages/notes/src returns only :52 and :287). samples.summary: note-sync now opens a Yorkie `doc.update` on EVERY docChanged ViewUpdate, including read-only mounts reacting to remote changes
samples.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/note-sync.ts:61 wraps the whole loop in `this.store.batch(() => {...})`, and `YorkieNoteStore.batch()` (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:76) unconditionally calls `this.doc.update(...)` before any transaction filtering. The out-of-diff consumer is packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:91, whose comment records the invariant that read-only share viewers must not issue writes ('a read-only share viewer has no write permission — the auth webhook would reject the update'). The current caller, packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-toolbar.tsx:200 (`canFormat = !readOnly && mode !== 'view'`), hides the buttons, so the bypass is not reachable today — but the guard added in this change is inconsistent across entry points and a future host calling `editor.undo()` would write on a read-only share.

finding.summary: note-sync now opens a Yorkie `doc.update` on EVERY docChanged ViewUpdate, including read-only mounts reacting to remote changes
finding.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/note-sync.ts:61 wraps the whole loop in `this.store.batch(() => {...})`, and `YorkieNoteStore.batch()` (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:76) unconditionally calls `this.doc.update(...)` before any transaction filtering. Previously, a read-only mount could never reach `doc.update` from this plugin: `editText` was only called for non-remote user-event transactions, which a non-editable view cannot produce. The out-of-diff consumer is packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:91, whose comment records the invariant that read-only share viewers must not issue writes ('a read-only share viewer has no write permission — the auth webhook would reject the update'). Now every peer edit or snapshot arriving at a read-only viewer opens a local (empty) update. Mitigating: `setLocalSelection` (remote-selection.ts:115) already calls doc.update on read-only mounts for presence, and the task note claims an empty update pushes nothing — hence low confidence. Fix belongs in YorkieNoteStore.batch (skip doc.update when nothing will be written) or in note-sync (only open a batch when at least one local transaction survives the filter).

verdict.reason: The mechanism exists (note-sync.ts:61 -> yorkie-note-store.ts:78 opens doc.update on every docChanged update, including remote-only ones), but the invariant it is said to violate does not hold in this repo and nothing downstream is left broken. The sibling plugin noteRemoteSelections is installed unconditionally next to noteSync (editor.ts:300-303; the only readOnly gating is EditorView.editable at :287 and historyKeymap at :213), and its update() calls store.setLocalSelection on EVERY ViewUpdate in both branches (remote-selection.ts:109-118), which reaches this.doc.update(...) at yorkie-note-store.ts:193. That is a strictly stronger write (a presence change is a real Yorkie change that is pushed) and it fires on the exact same remote-driven dispatches from applyRemote, so read-only mounts already open doc.update on every peer edit and snapshot today. The new batch, by contrast, produces no operations at all when every transaction is filtered out: yorkie-note-store.test.ts:95-99 exercises this against a real @yorkie-js/sdk Document and asserts an empty batch records nothing. The cited invariant at notes-view.tsx:89-91 is narrower than represented -- it guards ensureText(doc), which performs an actual seed write (r.content = new Text(), notes-view.tsx:53-56), not a no-op update. No caller is broken, no write reaches the server that did not before, and no guard is bypassed; the only residual is a per-remote-change context allocation, a perf nit below this lens's blocking bar.
